requirement:
The Markdown outline MUST expose colon-fenced directive containers and fenced
code blocks as anonymous `block` nodes using the shared anonymous-selector
rules under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. A block MUST
include its opening fence, body, and closing fence when present, and MUST be
nested under its nearest enclosing outline container.
rationale:
No test in the project covers `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fenced_blocks`. A `references` query for {test} sites on `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.*` returned none. The only reference to the subject is a {cite} from the Outlines section of `md/requirements/references.md`.

I also searched the crates for tests that exercise the behaviour without a marker. The searches covered `:::` and fence strings, `block@` and `kind[block]`. The Markdown outline tests in `crates/habeas-sdk/src/outline/tests.rs` are:
- `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` uses only a front-matter block, headings, a paragraph and an HTML comment. It has no colon-fenced container and no fenced code block.
- `markdown_hashes_include_paragraph_text_between_punctuation_tokens` is a paragraph-hash test.
- `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` is about comments.
- `no_profile_invents_fallback_kinds` only asserts that no generic `block` fallback kind appears. It does not check for fence blocks.

The requirement contains these untested obligations:
- Colon-fenced directive containers, such as `:::{note}`, MUST appear as anonymous `block` nodes. No test checks this.
- Fenced code blocks MUST appear as anonymous `block` nodes. No test checks this.
- Block selectors MUST use the `block@hash` form, with `#N` to separate identical siblings. No test checks this.
- A block MUST include its opening fence, body and closing fence when present. No test checks the node range, including an unclosed fence.
- A block MUST be nested under its nearest enclosing outline container. This covers a block directly under a section, a block inside another colon-fenced block, and a block inside a section. No test checks any of these.

A plausible violating implementation would give a block a range that omits the closing fence. It could also use another kind name, or hoist nested blocks to the section level. The reviewed tests would accept all of these.

text: The Markdown outline MUST expose colon-fenced directive containers and fenced
code blocks as anonymous `block` nodes using the shared anonymous-selector
include its opening fence, body, and closing fence when present, and MUST be
nested under its nearest enclosing outline container.
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
